title: Execution path chaotic switching: hardening plan and canary/rollback strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A mid-February scheduler rollout introduced probabilistic kernel probing that in mixed-quant and heterogeneous-batch workloads caused rapid execution-path switching. Symptoms were elevated p95/p99 latencies and 15-30% throughput regression for some model slices. This ticket captures the hardening plan, short-term mitigations already applied, and a formal canary/rollback strategy for future scheduler changes.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-18: New scheduler probe heuristic merged to main (PR #5432) and gradually rolled out to canary tenants.

2026-02-22: On 10% fleet rollout observed intermittent p95 spikes for mixed-quant models; automatic rollback to previous kernel selector occurred for some hosts but not others due to stale gating config.
2026-02-23: Pager triggered for throughput regressions affecting two enterprise customers; on-call team applied manual affinity pinning to affected pools.
2026-02-24: Hotfix deployed that reduced probe frequency and added a short hysteresis window, which restored baseline throughput for most workloads.
2026-03-05: Retrospective kickoff; root-cause analysis identified lack of hysteresis, insufficient telemetry on transient kernel switch events, and weak canary gating criteria.
2026-03-10: This ticket opened to track engineering remediation, tests, and canary policy updates.
root_cause: Probe-driven kernel selector introduced frequent probes without stateful hysteresis leading to oscillation across two incompatible kernel paths for certain sequence-length / quantization combinations.
Telemetry did not capture short-lived switch counts per request, so the regression surface was noisy and hard to correlate with changes in the scheduler policy.
Canary rollout gate used only host-level success rates; it did not measure per-model per-route latency divergence nor detect increased KV cache churn caused by path switching.
mitigations_applied: Reduced probe frequency and introduced a 200ms soft-hysteresis window in the scheduler (hotfix runtime-2.3.1) — immediate traffic stabilized.
Manually pinned affected enterprise pools to the previous kernel selection configuration while diagnostics ran.
Enabled extra verbose telemetry for 5% of hosts to capture kernel switch events and per-request KV cache miss metrics.
Customer-facing postmortem shared with impacted customers and support runbook updated with rollback steps.
decisions: Adopt a stable-first selection policy: prefer the last-used kernel path for N subsequent requests unless a statistically significant better path is detected across an evaluation window.
Require three observability signals for canary progression: per-route p95, kernel-switch-rate, and KV-cache-miss-rate (all relative to baseline).
Implement an automated rollback circuit-breaker that opens when canary signals deviate above thresholds for a configurable window.
action_items: (OWNER: Marco Li) Implement scheduler hysteresis with adjustable window and an opt-in shorter window for low-latency slices — due 2026-03-20.
(OWNER: Priya Nair) Add kernel-switch counters and per-request KV-cache churn telemetry to the runtime diagnostics pipeline and wire to console dashboards — due 2026-03-18.
(OWNER: Owen Park) Build a synthetic mixed-quant benchmark harness that exercises path-switching scenarios and include it in CI gating for scheduler PRs — due 2026-03-25.
(OWNER: Lina Gomez) Define canary gating policy document and implement the three-signal healthcheck in the canary orchestration system (include false-positive mitigation) — due 2026-03-22.
(OWNER: Security) Verify no sensitive customer data is included in verbose telemetry; confirm compliance for longer retention of diagnostics for postmortem — due 2026-03-16.
(OWNER: SRE oncall) Create a quick rollback runbook snippet that can be executed automatically if circuit-breaker trips, and add to PagerDuty escalation — due 2026-03-15.
acceptance_criteria: New CI benchmark shows <2% regression for mixed-quant synthetic suite vs baseline before merging changes to scheduler main branch.
Console dashboard displays kernel-switch-rate and KV-cache churn per-route; alerts fire when thresholds breached during canary rollouts.
Canary orchestration enforces three-signal gating and performs automated rollback within 5 minutes of sustained breach.
Post-deployment monitoring window for runtime-2.4 shows p95 within historical variance for 14-day evaluation on a 10% canary fleet.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for scheduler hysteresis logic covering edge cases and concurrent probe events.
Integration test that replays recorded production traces and verifies that hysteresis prevents oscillation under identical trace patterns.
E2E canary run in staging with synthetic traffic that mixes quantized and fp16 models at varying batch sizes to validate gating thresholds.
followups: Quarterly review to assess whether hysteresis parameters should be workload-specific or globally tuned.
Investigate whether KV-cache-aware kernel selection (prefer path that preserves cache locality) is feasible without compromising memory footprint.
Evaluate adding per-model A/B evaluations to detect quality regressions introduced by forced kernel affinity changes.
